neoConfucianism.definition: Updated Chinese philosophy that rejects Daoism and Buddhism

civilServiceExam.definition: First system of merit based government positions
civilServiceExam.effect: Grew and maintained dynastic imperial bureaucracy

filialPiety.definition: Respect for elders and authority figures
filialPiety.effect: Enforcement of strict social hierarchy in China

champaRice.definition: A quickly growing, drought resistant crop
champaRice.effect: Increased food production, causing Chinese population boom

songDynasty.definition: Chinese dynasty between the Tang and Yuan Dynasties
songDynasty.effect: Era of Chinese innovation: printing, gunpowder, paper money, navy, Champa rice, Neo-Confucianism

khanate.definition: State or society ruled by a khan; organized tribally
khanate.effect: Mongol Empire became the Yuan Dynasty, Ilkhanate, Chagatai Khanate, and Golden Horde

paxMongolica.definition: A period of stability throughout the Mongol Empire
paxMongolica.effect: Enabled safe long distance trade: spread ideas and the Bubonic Plague

sinification.definition: Process by which non-Chinese societies assimilate Chinese culture
sinification.effect: Fusion of cultures; unity across Asia and loss of some Asian cultural diversity

shogunate.definition: A government ruled by a shōgun, but nominally under an emperor
shogunate.effect: United Japan under the feudal system and a militaristic government

shinto.definition: Japanese polytheistic and animistic nature religion
shinto.effect: Legitimized rulers through belief in kami (supernatural entities)

bushido.effect: Encouraged the loyalty and filial piety of samurai; included elements of bureaucratic roles

goryeo.definition: A Korean state that unified and ruled the Korean Peninsula
goryeo.effect: Achieved true national unification of Korea; valued education, culture, and trade

yuanDynasty.definition: Chinese dynasty between the Song and Ming Dynasties
yuanDynasty.effect: Flourishing of culture and trade despite Mongol ruler

mingDynasty.definition: Chinese dynasty between the Yuan and Qing Dynasties
mingDynasty.effect: Last Han ruled Chinese dynasty; expanded trade and ties with the West

minamotoNoYoritomo.definition: The founder and first shogun of the Kamukara Shogunate
minamotoNoYoritomo.effect: Began the feudal age of Japan

genghisKhan.definition: The founder and first khan of the Mongol Empire
genghisKhan.effect: Formed and ruled the largest contiguous empire in history

kublaiKhan.definition: The founder and first emperor of the Yuan Dynasty
kublaiKhan.effect: The first non-Han emperor to rule all of China

marcoPolo.definition: An Italian traveler that gave Europeans a look at the Eastern world
marcoPolo.effect: First European to create a detailed account of his experience in East Asia

ibnBattuta.definition: A Moroccan Islamic traveler who wrote The Rihla
ibnBattuta.effect: The most traveled pre-modern explorer, whose book depicts most of Afro-Eurasia

zhenghe.definition: Chinese mariner, explorer, diplomat, and admiral
zhenghe.effect: Led Chinese naval expeditions to greatly increase China’s overseas influence

transSaharanTrade.definition: Trade across the Sahara Desert between Sub-Saharan and North Africa
transSaharanTrade.effect: Economic expansion of Africa; spread Islam

caravanserai.definition: Roadside inns for travelers along major trade routes
caravanserai.effect: Supported the flow of goods, and ideas along overland trade routes

sufism.definition: Mystic body of religious practice in Islam
sufism.effect: Spread Islam through missionary and educational activities

diaspora.definition: A population scattered and separated from geographic origin
diaspora.effect: Job opportunities, slavery, fleeing from persecution, etc

quran.effect: Guided the Islamic Empire and Muslims' way of life; influences Arab culture

sunniVsShia.effect: Cause of tensions, violence, and wars throughout history

caliphate.definition: Region under the leadership of a caliph (religious/political successor to Muhammad)
caliphate.effect: Formed massive empires that advanced and preserved science, literature, and Islam

sultanate.definition: Region under the rule of a sultan (Muslim sovereign)
sultanate.effect: More structured and smaller designation of Islamic state that replaced caliphates

houseOfWisdom.definition: Major public academy and intellectual center in Baghdad
houseOfWisdom.effect: Helped preserve and build upon European Classical era texts

seljukEmpire.definition: Turkic Muslim dynasty that ruled from the Middle East to Central Asia
seljukEmpire.effect: Islamic sultanates became controlled by Turks; contributed to Turco-Persian culture

mamlukSultanate.definition: Islamic sultanate led by a military caste of former slaves
mamlukSultanate.effect: Halted Mongol expansion; created a period of prosperity in the Middle East

timuridEmpire.definition: Persianate Turco-Mongol empire comprising much of Central Asia
timuridEmpire.effect: Had a small Islamic Renaissance; eventually led to creation of the Mughal Empire

urdu.definition: Indo-Aryan language spoken mostly in South Asia; combined Hindi and Persian
urdu.effect: Spoken throughout India; evidence of cultural blending

angkorWat.effect: Largest religious complex in the world; shows religious change in S.E. Asia

tamerlane.effect: Founded the Timurid Empire (which fragmented after him); fearsome military leader

battleOfBachDang.definition: Last major battle between the Mongols and Dai Viet + Champa
battleOfBachDang.effect: Major Vietnamese victory which ended Yuan southward expansion

delhiSultanate.definition: Islamic late medieval empire stretching across the Indian subcontinent
delhiSultanate.effect: Established Islamic presence in the Indian subcontinent; succeeded by the Mughal Empire

khmerEmpire.definition: A Hindu-Buddhist empire in what is now Cambodia, Laos, and Thailand
khmerEmpire.effect: Source of religious art, culture, and architecture like Angkor Wat

srivijayaEmpire.definition: Buddhist maritime empire based on the island of Sumatra
srivijayaEmpire.effect: Held its power through trade and controlled the Strait of Malacca

majapahitEmpire.definition: Hindu-Buddhist maritime empire based on the island of Java
majapahitEmpire.effect: The empire resisted Yuan influence, controlled regional trade, and covered most of Southeast Asia

aztecEmpire.definition: An alliance of the Mexico-Tenochtitlan, Tetzcoco, and Tlacopan city-states
aztecEmpire.effect: Waged wars of conquest to gain tributary states; fell to the Spanish

mexica.definition: A Nahuatl-speaking people that ruled the Aztec Empire
mexica.effect: Built a massive empire and Tenochtitlan; conquered by the Spanish

tenochtitlan.definition: The capital of the Aztec Empire, present day Mexico City
tenochtitlan.effect: Most populous city of the Aztec Empire; led the Aztecs politically

chinampas.definition: An agricultural technique using small rectangular areas of land on shallow lake beds

cahokia.definition: The site of the largest and most influential city of Native American Mississippian culture

incaEmpire.definition: The largest empire in pre-European America; heavily centralized
incaEmpire.effect: Thriving empire that developed in isolation, without writing, iron, or money; fell to the Spanish

chasqui.definition: A messenger of the Inca Empire, highly trained and agile
chasqui.effect: Transported messages in the form of quipo, oral information or small packets

quipo.definition: An information recording device consisting of colored threads with knots
quipo.effect: Stored information for Inca Empire, which had no writing system

mita.definition: An Incan system using labor as a tax
mita.effect: Helped the Incan government maintain its power and make public service and military projects

puebloans.definition: Native Americans in present-day Southwestern United States

greatZimbabwe.definition: A medieval city in Zimbabwe surrounded by a large stone wall
greatZimbabwe.effect: Contributed to the development of Sub-Saharan Africa, but declined due to overgrazing

timbuktu.definition: A city in West Africa, was part of the Mali and Songhai empires
timbuktu.effect: Became a center of Islamic scholarship and grew wealthy from its gold-salt trade

ethiopianEmpire.definition: A uniquely Christian empire in Eastern Africa
ethiopianEmpire.effect: Maintained an isolated branch of Christianity despite being surrounded by Islamic empires

swahili.definition: A Bantu language spoken primarily along the East African coast
swahili.effect: Major part of culture and trade along the East African coast

berbers.definition: Grouping of distinct ethnic groups indigenous to North Africa
berbers.effect: Founded and were a part of many African empires

bantuMigrations.definition: Series of migrations of the Bantu people from Central to sub-Saharan Africa
bantuMigrations.effect: Spread of Bantu culture, innovations in metallurgy and agriculture throughout Africa

hausaKingdoms.definition: A collection of states started by the Hausa people
hausaKingdoms.effect: Contained powerful city states that were centers of trade and production

maliEmpire.definition: A West African empire renowned for the wealth of its rulers
maliEmpire.effect: Contained cities that were centers of trade and Islamic scholarship

feudalism.definition: Political system in which land is distributed in exchange for service
feudalism.effect: Localized communities, lowering social mobility and innovation

serfdom.definition: System of peasants being tied directly to the land they work on
serfdom.effect: Low social mobility for the majority; enforced agricultural production

hanseaticLeague.definition: A medieval confederation of merchant guilds in Northern Europe
hanseaticLeague.effect: Expanded and developed trade by reducing tolls and making trade safer

magnaCarta.definition: A charter defining rights for barons and lords in England
magnaCarta.effect: One of the first documents regulating the authority of a ruler

crusades.definition: A series of religious wars facilitated by the Catholic Church
crusades.effect: Increased the power of the Catholic Church; led to contact between Europe and others

blackDeath.definition: The most fatal pandemic ever recorded

littleIceAge.definition: Period of regional cooling in the North Atlantic region
littleIceAge.effect: Long term agricultural crisis and famine, made travel more difficult

byzantineEmpire.definition: The continuation of the Roman Empire's eastern half
byzantineEmpire.effect: Was the most powerful force in the Mediterranean region during its existence

kievanRus.definition: A group of principalities ruled by the Rurik dynasty
kievanRus.effect: Spread Christianity to North Eastern Europe; fell to the Mongols

hundredYearsWar.definition: A series of armed conflicts fought between the kingdoms of England and France
hundredYearsWar.effect: French victory led to the strengthening of the monarchy and the loss of British territory

margeryKempe.definition: A Christian mystic/pilgrim who traveled to holy sites

ibnSina.definition: A philosopher and physician of the Muslim world
ibnSina.effect: The father of early modern medicine

nasirAlDinAlTusi.definition: A Persian polymath who made significant mathematical advancements
nasirAlDinAlTusi.effect: Invented trigonometry, made significant contributions to astronomy

rumi.definition: A Sufi mystic, Islamic scholar, poet, and theologian
rumi.effect: Has had a global literary influence based on his Islamic poetry

ibnKhaldun.definition: An Arab sociologist, philosopher, and historian
ibnKhaldun.effect: The father of historiography, sociology, economics, and demography studies

aishaAlBauniyya.definition: A female Sufi mystic and poet/author
aishaAlBauniyya.effect: She wrote more works in Arabic than any other women in the medieval period

pachacuti.definition: The first emperor of the expanded Incan Empire
pachacuti.effect: Vastly expanded the Chiefdom of Cusco into the huge Incan Empire

montezumaII.definition: The ninth Emperor of the Aztec Empire
montezumaII.effect: Ruled the Aztecs at their peak and during their fall to the Spanish

sundiataKieta.definition: The founder and first Mansa of the Mali Empire

mansaMusa.definition: The ninth Mansa of the Mali Empire and the richest person ever
mansaMusa.effect: Went on a famous Hajj to Mecca that made the Mali Empire famous; promoted Islam

gutenberg.definition: German inventor and craftsman who invented the movable-type printing press
gutenberg.effect: Began an information revolution and mass-spread of literature in Europe

judaism.definition: First abrahamic, monotheistic, and ethnic religion

christianity.definition: Abrahamic monotheistic religion centered on the Bible
christianity.effect: Religion spread worldwide through heavy imperialism
christianity.continent: south america, north america, europe, asia, africa, oceania

islam.definition: Abrahamic monotheistic religion centered on the Quran
islam.effect: Dominant religion in Africa and the Middle East

hinduism.definition: Indian religion based around dharma (the universal order)
hinduism.effect: Dominant religion in India, dividing people into castes

buddhism.definition: Indian religion based on teachings of the Buddha
buddhism.effect: Religion spread by merchants and travelers along trade networks
